hook: Tripathi has spent his career on the unglamorous but consequential work of making health data actually move between systems, first from the policy side as the U.S. government's top health IT official, and now from inside a leading hospital system, applying that same interoperability and governance discipline to how AI gets deployed in clinical care.
name: Micky Tripathi

quote.text: Trust in AI in health care will be earned through transparency, not assumed through technology.
quote.context: A recurring theme in Tripathi's public remarks and ONC policy statements on health AI transparency, 2023-2024

moniker: Federal Architect of Health AI Policy

reading.body:
Micky Tripathi is the person most directly responsible for the first federal transparency requirement for clinical AI algorithms, and he now applies that same governance framework from inside a major hospital system.

His career follows a single through-line: making health data move reliably between institutions, and setting rules for what happens when software interposes itself in that flow. The 2004 work building regional health information exchange in Massachusetts, the 2021 appointment as the federal government's top health-IT official, and the 2024 finalization of the HTI-1 rule are all expressions of the same discipline. HTI-1 is notable in this record not as a general AI policy statement but as a targeted requirement: certified electronic health record systems must disclose how their embedded predictive algorithms work. That is a specific, operational definition of transparency, applied to a specific class of software.

His move to Mayo Clinic in 2024 matters because it collapses the distance between rulemaking and deployment. The data does not say how Mayo Clinic is using AI, which specific algorithms are governed under his oversight there, or what outcomes have followed. It records only that the person who wrote the federal rules is now the one deciding how a leading health system implements them.

The data does not connect Tripathi's work to compute infrastructure, data center construction, or power supply. His domain is governance and interoperability standards, which are upstream of deployment decisions but not upstream of the physical infrastructure that makes large-scale clinical AI run.
